title: Next-Gen Education: Enhancing AI for Microlearning
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 ASEE Annual Conference & Exposition
extended_summary:
This paper addresses whether AI-generated microlearning materials can support student learning in higher education and how accurate such materials are when produced by large language models. The authors frame the problem around low attendance, limited student engagement with long recorded lectures, and the time burden on educators who might otherwise create supplementary microlearning content manually. They focus on two research questions: how students perceive the effectiveness of AI-generated microlearning for learning and engagement, and how accurate students find the AI-produced content.

The intervention is an AI-supported pipeline that converts lecture videos and slides into microlearning materials. Using OpenAI Whisper to transcribe lecture videos and ChatGPT/GPT-4o to refine transcripts and generate content, the system produces interactive quizzes, digital flashcards, mini-lessons, and scenario-based learning activities. The paper also includes a case study demonstrating the pipeline on a 22-minute lecture about pointers in C programming, showing sample prompts and generated outputs. In addition, the authors computed readability scores for the generated materials.

The empirical study was conducted in two junior-level computer science courses at Pennsylvania State University in the United States: Discrete Mathematics and Programming Language Principles. The combined enrollment was 650 undergraduate students in hybrid courses with both in-person and recorded lectures. Microlearning materials were integrated throughout a semester, with different frequencies and grading policies across the two courses. At the end of the semester, 360 students completed surveys about learning efficiency, engagement, usefulness as a starting point, perceived inaccuracies, and alignment with course content.

The main conclusions are that students generally viewed the AI-generated microlearning materials positively, especially for time efficiency, engagement, and as a starting point for learning new topics. Programming Language Principles showed stronger positive responses than Discrete Mathematics, suggesting that microlearning may fit application-oriented subjects better than more abstract ones. Students reported relatively few inaccuracies, and most judged the materials as relevant to course content, but the authors emphasize that human review remains necessary. Overall, the paper concludes that AI-enhanced microlearning is a scalable and promising support strategy in higher education, while also noting the importance of instructor oversight and subject-specific adaptation.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI/chatbot family used for text generation and transformation tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to refine Whisper-generated lecture transcripts and generate AI-based microlearning materials from lecture videos and slides, including flashcards, quizzes, mini-lessons/summaries, and scenario-based learning activities for two junior-level computer science courses.

findings.finding_summary: Student survey responses indicated generally positive perceived learning efficiency from the ChatGPT-generated microlearning materials. Aggregated across both courses, Time Efficiency had mean=4.04 (SD=0.92), Improved Retention had mean=3.70 (SD=0.95), and Interactive Learning had mean=3.71 (SD=0.97); these were self-reported perceptions rather than objective performance measures.
findings.measure: Student self-reported perceptions of learning efficiency, including time efficiency, improved retention, and interactive learning

findings.finding_summary: Students reported positive engagement with the AI-generated microlearning content. In Discrete Mathematics, approximately 67% either agreed or strongly agreed that the content supported engagement, compared with 80% in Programming Language Principles; disagreement was 8% (7 students) and 4% (12 students), respectively.
findings.measure: Student self-reported engagement with course content supported by AI-generated microlearning

findings.finding_summary: Students generally viewed the ChatGPT-generated microlearning as a useful starting point for learning new topics. More than 65% of students in Discrete Mathematics and more than 80% in Programming Language Principles agreed or strongly agreed; disagreement was 7% (6 students) and 5% (13 students), respectively.
findings.measure: Student self-reported value of microlearning as a starting point for learning new topics

findings.finding_summary: Students reported that inaccuracies were present but relatively infrequent in the AI-generated materials. Over 35% of students in both courses reported never encountering incorrect information, while more than 40% in Discrete Mathematics and over 50% in Programming Language Principles reported encountering incorrect information 1 to 3 times; instructor anecdotal review found fewer than 10 inaccuracies across all generated materials.
findings.measure: Student-reported frequency of inaccuracies in AI-generated instructional content

findings.finding_summary: Students largely judged the AI-generated microlearning content to be relevant and aligned with course material. In Discrete Mathematics, 76.5% responded 'Yes', 18.5% 'Maybe', and 4.9% 'No'; in Programming Language Principles, 87.1% responded 'Yes', 11.1% 'Maybe', and 1.8% 'No'.
findings.measure: Student-reported relevance/alignment of AI-generated content with actual course materials

findings.finding_summary: The AI pipeline using ChatGPT and related OpenAI tools substantially reduced content production time. The paper reports that 150 to 225 minutes of lecture video and over 100 pages of lecture slides could be processed into microlearning materials within about 45 minutes for each assignment.
findings.measure: Time required to process lecture videos and slides into microlearning materials

identified_tools.name: Whisper
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's automatic speech recognition model for speech-to-text transcription.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to transcribe recorded lecture videos as the first step in the microlearning-generation pipeline.

findings.finding_summary: Whisper enabled automated transcription of lecture videos for downstream microlearning generation, but the paper reports several transcription problems. The authors observed grammatical errors, improper word usage, unclear passages, and some inaccurately transcribed segments due to poor recording quality, which necessitated subsequent transcript refinement with ChatGPT.
findings.measure: Observed transcription quality and usability of lecture video transcripts

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical deployment study with survey-based evaluation across two university courses, but it relies primarily on descriptive self-reported perceptions rather than validated causal designs or objective learning outcomes. No RCT, quasi-experimental comparison, or effect-size-based achievement analysis is reported.
impact_tier_rationale: Findings are generally positive for perceived engagement, efficiency, and relevance, and operational time savings are substantial, but impact on actual academic performance is unclear because no objective outcome effects or standardized effect sizes are reported.
